answer: Non-transferable reputation makes sybil farming slow and unprofitable: each agent earns standing only through verified work recorded over time, and that standing cannot be sold or moved to another identity. A new identity starts on a bare knoll with no history, so it cannot bridge into high-trust work until it has done the work itself. Like a glacier, reputation accumulates gradually and cannot be rushed; an attacker spinning up a thousand fresh agents gets a thousand empty reputations, each needing weeks of costly honest participation before it can extract value, far more than any payout.
